name: New Brunswick: public health coverage for newcomers
name_fr: Nouveau-Brunswick : assurance maladie publique pour les nouveaux arrivants
description: Who is covered by New Brunswick Medicare by immigration status, any waiting period for newcomers, how to apply, the public drug-coverage model and the share of adults with a regular health care provider.

attributes.legal_status: in force (eligibility rules as published on the access date)

eligibility_by_status.citizen: Eligible as a resident (residency and presence rules apply).
eligibility_by_status.permanent_resident: Eligible if legally entitled to remain in Canada and making a permanent home in New Brunswick, with no intention to keep PR status in another country.
eligibility_by_status.work_permit_holder: Work permits are listed among accepted immigration documents, but 'not all Canadian immigration documents are acceptable'; no duration rule given.
eligibility_by_status.study_permit_holder: Eligible with a study permit valid for the full school year (at least September–April); exchange, part-time and certain graduate students excluded.
eligibility_by_status.visitor: Visitors and tourists are expressly excluded in the AB, MB, NB and PE material read; treat visitors as not covered everywhere and confirm locally.

attributes.status_dependency: Which rule applies depends on the user's immigration status, which is unknown (USER-PROFILE.md: 'Citizenship(s) and current country of residence', 'Existing Canadian status or application').

newcomer_waiting_period.arriving_from_outside_canada: Newcomers from outside Canada 'may be entitled to Medicare coverage from their first day of arrival', once deemed to have established permanent residence.
newcomer_waiting_period.moving_from_another_province: First day of the third month after the month residence is established.

attributes.how_to_apply: Only after physically moving to NB: online Medicare application or PDF form (mail, email, Service New Brunswick).
attributes.drug_coverage_model: New Brunswick Drug Plan for uninsured residents with income-based premiums and co-payments; separate Prescription Drug Program for low-income seniors and others (PMPRB 2020/21 summary).

regular_provider.source: CIHI indicator 'Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider', Statistics Canada CCHS

sources.title: Canadians With a Primary Health Care Provider — indicator data table (data updated October 2026); underlying data: Statistics Canada, Canadian Community Health Survey, Annual Component
sources.methodology: Weighted percent of adults 18+ reporting a regular/primary health care provider (family doctor, nurse practitioner or other); 95% confidence interval given. 2025 adult questions were harmonized, so compare with earlier years with caution.

sources.title: Public Drug Plan Designs, 2021/22 edition (describes 2020/21 plan designs; page modified 2024-01-30)

verification.notes: Provincial page(s) fetched directly where status is 'verified'; otherwise some content came from search-engine extracts of official pages (403 or bot-check on fetch). Regular-provider figures parsed from CIHI's published data table.

limitations: Eligibility text summarises official pages and is not legal advice; temporary-status rules change often. Drug-plan designs are from PMPRB's 2020/21 summary and may be out of date. 'Without a regular provider' is 100 minus the CIHI share (simple arithmetic).
